item.text: {"question_id":"1B.6","answer":"China maintained a formal nonproliferation and export-control framework during the period, including treaty participation, licensing, end-user and end-use certification, control lists, expert review, customs controls, interagency coordination, and investigation and legal handling of suspected violations (BATCH-0015-E006; BATCH-0017-E014; BATCH-0024-E002). In 2023, Chinese representatives also supported multilateral export controls and proposed safeguards-related processes while opposing AUKUS nuclear-submarine cooperation as a proliferation risk (BATCH-0016-E002; BATCH-0017-E004; BATCH-0023-E004). These are favorable evidence of stated policy, institutional arrangements, and diplomatic conduct, but the supplied record does not independently establish their effectiveness, identify a 2023 case involving an ally, proxy, client, firm, military-linked entity, or domestic faction, or show that Xi personally directed corrective action after monitoring exposed evasion or assistance. The answer therefore supports formal control capacity and nonproliferation commitments, while leaving operational enforcement, monitoring quality, and ruler-level response substantially uncertain.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0017-E004","BATCH-0017-E014","BATCH-0023-E004","BATCH-0024-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The formal systems are described primarily in official sources and are not independently audited in the supplied record.","No named 2023 enforcement outcome, sanction, or corrective response involving an ally, proxy, client, firm, military-linked entity, or domestic faction is supplied.","The evidence does not establish Xi's personal authorship or intervention in the framework's implementation.","BATCH-0024-E001 and BATCH-0024-E002 are later-updated summaries of policies accumulated over multiple years, so their 2023 temporal fit is partial."] ,"corrections_made":["Qualified 'established' as a formal framework and avoided treating official descriptions as proof of effective enforcement.","Removed the weakly relevant military-civil-fusion and nuclear-modernization material from the contrary evidence.","Restored treaty-inventory evidence and retained the AUKUS safeguards position as contextual diplomatic evidence.","Preserved the distinction between stated policy, institutional capacity, verified enforcement, and ruler-level corrective action."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A named 2023 or ruler-period enforcement case could materially change the assessment of actual control and response.","Independent evidence on Chinese export-control compliance, evasion monitoring, or action against state-linked entities is needed to resolve the main uncertainty."]}
